transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-11-02
Start time: 15:00 PT
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Li (Redwood SE), Carlos Vega (CTO - BlueMarlin), Anya Rios (Lead ML Eng), Samir Patel (Infra), Lena Ortiz (Product)

Summary:
Quick discovery focused on p95 latency targets for streaming responses, concurrency and token/sec throughput for an account reconciliation assistant at BlueMarlin. Interest in comparing Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC) for predictable SLOs and data residency.

Topics:
- p95 latency objectives (streaming & non-streaming)
- concurrency and burst behavior (peak tokens/sec)
- profiling harness and pilot design
- security (SOC 2, KMS, VPC) and rollout timeline

Transcript:
[00:00:00] Maya (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intros, then we'll jump into your workload. Carlos, do you want to kick off with the high level?
[00:00:12] Carlos (BlueMarlin): Sure, yeah. We're building an assistant that helps our ops staff reconcile delayed shipments, it's heavy on doc context and step-by-step streaming replies. We're seeing spikes in requests around cutover windows, so p95 is really critical — we need to be under 350ms for the streaming first-token p95 ideally.
[00:00:35] Ethan (Redwood): Okay p95 first-token 350ms, got it. Is that end-to-end or just model inference?
[00:00:40] Carlos: End-to-end, the UX folks measure perceived latency from the user event to first token. We can tolerate a slightly higher tail for full completion but first token is the focus.
[00:00:47] Anya (BlueMarlin): Also want to note, some responses are long — 800 to 2k tokens — so throughput matters. During batch reconciles we could hit sustained 12k tokens/sec across the cluster. Peak bursts though, like manual troubleshooting, can be 25k tokens/sec for 30–90 seconds.
[00:01:04] Maya: That's helpful. Are you currently running any on-prem inference or is this all cloud?
[00:01:09] Samir (BlueMarlin): Mostly cloud but security wants a VPC private option. For pilot we can start hosted but long term they prefer Dedicated in our VPC or even a private install behind our firewall. We need KMS integration too.
[00:01:22] Ethan: Understood. On the hosting side we can usually hit low p95s with streaming using our optimizations, but if you need reserved capacity for sustained token throughput Dedicated gives predictable unit economics.
[00:01:34] Lena (BlueMarlin): What about fallback? If Dedicated is saturated do you fall back to Hosted or a smaller model?
[00:01:40] Maya: We have routing policies — can fail over to hosted or to a quantized, lower-cost variant depending on your policy. We can show you cost/latency tradeoffs.
[00:01:48] Carlos: For compliance, we need audit logs, per-request tracing, and retention controls. Are those in the console?
[00:01:54] Ethan: Yes, Console has per-request tracing, token-level cost breakdowns and audit logs. For private deployments we can integrate with your audit pipeline and push logs to your SIEM.
[00:02:03] Anya: I'd like to get into the specifics of how you measure p95. Are you measuring on the model node or at the edge? We've seen vendors report different numbers based on where they instrument.
[00:02:12] Ethan: Good question. Our internal p95 for streaming is from request receipt at our edge to first token emitted by the model runtime. For E2E you should include network transit, client-side processing, and front-end buffering. We can provide both numbers.
[00:02:25] Anya: Perfect. Also curious about KV cache behavior with long conversations — do you evict aggressively? We've had context windows where kv cash (sic) thrashes.
[00:02:34] Ethan: We do smart KV cache retention and prefix caching across common prompts. There can be edge cases though, we'll walk the cache strategy in the profiling workshop.
[00:02:42] [00:02:45] Carlos: Walk us through a typical pilot you run for latency/throughput discovery.
[00:02:48] Maya: Sure — usually step 1 we ask for representative prompt sets and traffic traces. Step 2 Redwood runs a pre-profile on hosted to get baseline p95 and tokens/sec. Then we propose a short Dedicated pilot where we reserve a few GPUs and run your traffic pattern and token-streaming benchmarks. We measure p50/p95/p99 for first token and full completion and then iterate on batching/quant configs.
[00:03:10] Samir: For the pilot we'd need a harness we can run in our environment too. Can you provide an open-source harness?
[00:03:16] Ethan: Yes — we'll share a sample bench harness (python + k6 steps) that can emulate streaming and token rates. It also supports KV cache priming. We'll include instructions for both hosted and VPC runs.
[00:03:27] Lena: Pricing — at what point does Dedicated make sense vs hosted? We don't want to overcommit.
[00:03:33] Maya: Typically if you have predictable sustained throughput and want consistent latency and capacity isolation, Dedicated or Reserved is better. We'll show a breakeven with your expected monthly tokens and burst profile. For unpredictable but low volume hosted is cheaper.
[00:03:47] Anya: Can you baseline the p95 for our typical reconciliation prompt? We have a few long prompts that include 30–40KB of docs. That seems like it blows up latency.
[00:03:56] Ethan: Large context increases tokenization and I/O. For truly large doc context we recommend a hybrid: pre-embed or chunking and a short context to the model at inference time. If you must send the full doc, expected p95 will be higher. We'll quantify with your prompts.
[00:04:12] [00:04:15] Carlos: We also have a hard requirement for P95 – 500ms for quick ops tasks and 1.5s for long-form analysis — are those realistic?
[00:04:23] Ethan: 500ms p95 for short replies in a multi-tenant hosted environment is aggressive but achievable depending on model choice and sequence length. Dedicated with optimized kernels gives better predictability. For long-form 1.5s p95 is generally attainable. We'll capture your target SLAs in the pilot plan.
[00:04:38] Samir: On the networking side, if we do VPC Private, what's the latency cost for cross-region? Our users are globally distributed, but primary cluster would be in us-west-2.
[00:04:47] Maya: Cross-region routing adds RTT; we recommend regional endpoints for low latency. We can provision Dedicated in us-west-2 and have failover in eu-west-1 if you need geo resiliency.
[00:04:58] Anya: For burst handling, do you use autoscaling or pre-warming? We saw cold starts cripple throughput on another vendor.
[00:05:04] Ethan: Both. Dedicated supports pre-warmed replicas and configurable autoscaling policies with burst capacity. For streaming use-cases we prefer pre-warmed pools to avoid cold-attention costs.
[00:05:15] Lena: How do you report tokens/sec? Is it per-node or aggregated? We need peak cluster capacity numbers.
[00:05:21] Ethan: We report both. The dashboard shows per-node token/sec and aggregated cluster token/sec. For capacity planning we provide guidance on node counts vs expected sustained and peak tokens/sec.
[00:05:32] Carlos: Any limits on concurrency per session? We have concurrent user sessions with multiple chat windows.
[00:05:37] Ethan: There's no hard per-session limit; we expose concurrency as a policy. For very high concurrency you should consider session-level sharding and state management to reduce KV pressure.
[00:05:47] Anya: Can you run a micro-benchmark with our prompts against a quantized 4-bit variant? We want to understand cost/latency trade-offs.
[00:05:54] Ethan: Absolutely — part of the pilot we can test standard FP16, INT8/4-bit quantized variants and report throughput, quality delta, and cost. We'll include an eval harness for quality checks.
[00:06:05] [00:06:10] Maya: Quick aside on observability — our console surfaces token-level cost by route and per-request latency heatmaps. We also support trace export to Jaeger or your APM.
[00:06:20] Samir: On security, we need SAML/SSO and role-based access — does Redwood Console support granular RBAC?
[00:06:26] Ethan: Yes SAML and OIDC and granular RBAC; for Private deployments you can sync with your IdP. We also support customer-managed KMS and HSM for key storage.
[00:06:36] Carlos: Any compliance docs we can share with procurement?
[00:06:39] Maya: We'll send the security deck and SOC2 attestation. If you need additional audits we'll coordinate through our security team.
[00:06:46] Lena: What about functional regressions — how do you guard model updates? We can't have sudden drops in important completion quality.
[00:06:52] Ethan: We do rollout policies: canary, A/B, and automatic rollback triggered by eval regressions tied to your prompt sets. Redwood Optimize can monitor quality metrics and alert on drift.
[00:07:03] Anya: Great. For the pilot benchmarks I'd like to see p50/p95/p99 and tokens/sec graphs with request distribution histograms.
[00:07:09] Ethan: We'll provide that. Also we'll include per-route cost breakdown to model cost tradeoffs.
[00:07:15] Carlos: Timeline — if we approve a pilot next week how quickly can you spin up a test cluster?
[00:07:20] Maya: For hosted baseline profiling we can start within 24–48 hours. For Dedicated pilot in your VPC expect 7–10 business days for provisioning and network setup. Private on-prem will take longer (depends on infra).
[00:07:32] Samir: For the VPC path, what's the network setup? Do you need open egress to your control plane?
[00:07:36] Ethan: For VPC Private we run a customer-controlled private control plane; there are options for direct peering or cross-connect. We'll send the network diagram.
[00:07:44] [00:07:47] Lena: Ok let's recap action items then.
[00:07:50] Maya: Sure — Redwood to send security deck and SOC2, Ethan to draft benchmark plan and harness, Redwood to send pricing and Dedicated vs Hosted cost breakeven, BlueMarlin to provide prompt sets and traffic traces, Samir to prep VPC networking contacts if pilot moves forward.
[00:08:05] Carlos: Sounds good. One more question — is there a recommended minimum node spec for the model family we plan to use? We're leaning toward an open LLM around 20B.
[00:08:15] Ethan: For a 20B family with streaming and low p95 you want GPUs with high memory bandwidth — we'll recommend instance types and quantization profiles. Also we'll include kernel optimization notes.
[00:08:26] Anya: Regarding quality tradeoffs on 4-bit quant, do you have previous eval numbers for similar tasks?
[00:08:31] Ethan: We have benchmark artifacts for typical instruction-following tasks; we'll include a reference but we'll always run your prompts to be safe.
[00:08:38] [00:08:41] Maya: Any blockers on your side for proceeding?
[00:08:44] Anya: None, just need to pull the prompt sets and get legal sign-off for a pilot NDA.
[00:08:50] Samir: I'll sync with networking to see if we can open a test VPC peering for the pilot — might take a week.
[00:08:56] Carlos: Procurement will also want cost predictability — we'll need the pricing bands as soon as possible.
[00:09:02] Maya: We'll prioritize that.
[00:09:05] Ethan: I'll put together the sample harness and preliminary profiling plan and attach it to the next email.
[00:09:11] Maya: Great — thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the security package and pilot proposal.
[00:09:16] Carlos: Thanks.

(Transcription notes: occasional mis-heard words like "kv cash" for KV cache, SAMS for SAML; timestamps approximate and there are brief crosstalk overlaps.)

End of transcript.
